**Finding: Compliant** — no redline proposed.

The agreement has a dedicated § 11 (Transition Assistance and Data Return) that satisfies the **preferred** position on all material terms:

| Playbook element | Document | Assessment |
|---|---|---|
| Transition assistance up to 6 months | 11.1 — six months at Customer's request | Met, and priced at rates in the expiring Order Form rather than "then-current rates" — better for us (no uplift exposure) |
| Data return within 30 days, machine-readable | 11.2 — thirty days, complete/commonly used/documented/machine-readable, with relationships and metadata; no withholding for fee disputes | Exceeds preferred |
| Deletion + certification thereafter | 11.3 — secure deletion of active systems and backups as they cycle, officer certification in writing | Met |

Two points worth noting affirmatively rather than as concerns:

- **Deletion sequencing is protective.** 11.3 is triggered only "After Customer confirms successful return," so the walk-away risk (immediate deletion on termination) is foreclosed. The Applicable Law retention carve-out is bounded — the retained copy stays protected and cannot be repurposed.
- **§ 10 does not cut across § 11.** 10.1 ends access only "after any agreed transition period" and preserves our rights in Customer Data; 10.2 adds Deliverable delivery and refunds of prepaid Fees.

One drafting nuance, flagged for awareness only and not a deviation: the 30-day clock in 11.2 runs from *Customer's request* rather than from termination, so we should make the return request promptly at exit. Similarly, 11.1 assistance is request-triggered. Both are consistent with the playbook's "at Customer's request" model language.
